(Democratic Republic of the Congo): Leveraging the German Cooperation's proven expertise in improving water service delivery, USAID will expand drinking water and basic sanitation access by improving local governance of the water sector. USAID will support the development of a strong and credible regulatory framework that clearly separates the policymaking (executive), regulatory, and service delivery functions within the water sector and strengthens the Provincial Water Services Authority in North Kivu, South Kivu, Kasai Oriental, and Lomami...With FY 2022 funds, USAID will work with the central-level Ministry of Hydraulic Resources and Electricity to establish and operationalize the national regulatory authority for the water sector, ensure compliance with applicable laws, standards, and contracts, establish a system for the arbitration of disputes, and monitor water prices. At the provincial level, FY 2022 funds will support setting, measuring, and enforcing standards of the Provincial Water Services Authority, build its capacity to fulfill its role as project owner, support an efficient operator organization for service management, and engage communities to increase their ownership and mitigate conflict...This activity will contribute to Mission Objective 2.2 (Expand U.S. investment and economic ties by supporting anti-corruption efforts, enhancing security, promoting transparent governance systems, establishing a more cost-effective regulatory framework, and enabling a more investor-friendly business environment) by supporting policy interventions and regulatory frameworks that facilitate private sector participation in water service delivery. Increased private sector engagement maximizes taxpayer investments and advances Administrator Power's Localization Agenda. Furthermore, this activity supports the U.S. Global Water Strategy, which defines water security as a national security priority...

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

description.narrative: Improve the capacity and sustainability of civil and criminal justice sector actors and institutions, enhance coordination amongst them, develop citizen demand for an effective and accountable justice system, and develop associations to advocate for all citizens. Work towards an equitable justice system by ensuring equality before the law, fair trial standards, and other elements of procedural fairness. Ensure more equitable access to justice through innovations within and beyond the state system and through improvements in the quality and quantity of justice services, with a particular focus on women, youth, the poor, and other marginalized or vulnerable groups. description.narrative: Supports the following illustrative program-funded costs: salaries of US, FSN, and TCN and other staff such as PSCs, RSSAs, PASAs, CASUs working for the US Government managing, administering, and supporting programs and their program-funded benefits such as housing, travel, transportation, education allowances etc; institutional contractors that provide such staff, rent, IT services, the program-funded share of utilities, staff training costs and the cost of developing and administering training programs, equipment and supplies, ICASS, vehicle fuel and maintenance, maintenance contracts, janitorial services, operational unit web page development and maintenance, outreach such as publications and the cost of their preparation (including staff costs), and technical assistance to ensure USG compliance with regulations.

DDR programs generally constitute integral components of war-to-peace transitions in post-conflict environments. DDR activities are designed to reduce or eliminate belligerent armed forces and the supply of armed weapons. In particular, USG interventions seek to facilitate the return of ex-combatants, including women and children associated with armed forces, to sustainable civilian livelihoods and ease their transition to civilian communities to secure sustainable peace.

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): .Through its Counter Gender-Based.Violence (C-GBV) activity, USAID will use FY 2021 funds to strengthen.communities' abilities to prevent and respond to gender-based violence (GBV),.reducing GBV incidences and providing access to holistic care for survivors,.including trafficked persons and other vulnerable groups. The activity provides.medical, legal, psychosocial, and economic support services to survivors.through village savings and loan associations, and training of social workers,.psychologists, medical personnel, community-based organizations, first.responders, and legal advocates. C-GBV invests in community awareness campaigns.to promote women's rights and community acceptance of GBV survivors..In concert with previously.obligated democracy and governance and economic support funds, FY 2021 health.funds will support vulnerable and marginalized groups such as LGBTI persons.affected by GBV and trafficking. Activities will include provision of family.planning commodities and services, social and behavior change communication,.and community-based trauma healing programs that shift community norms and.reduce stigma and negative attitudes that prevent GBV survivor reintegration..Family planning activities will also strengthen the capacity of Congolese.institutions and communities to deliver quality, integrated health services.that sustainably reduce maternal and child deaths, combat infectious diseases,.and increase access to voluntary family planning. The activity will promote.self-reliance of government entities to ensure results are sustained over the.long-term. .C-GBV contributes to Mission.Objective 3.1 of the Integrated Country Strategy ("Foundation for durable peace.strengthened in eastern DRC") by strengthening community-based prevention of,.and response to, sexual and gender-based violence. Interventions will be fully.integrated across a range of USAID activities and engage multiple stakeholders.to ensure optimal impact

title.narrative: Asili 2.0 - Scaling for Sustainability in the Kivus

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): .Asili 2.0 will provide access to basic sanitation services to 7,500 people while enabling 75,000 beneficiaries to obtain access to safe drinking water. FY 2021 funds will support USAID water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) objectives through a Global Development Alliance (GDA) with Alight (formerly the American Refugee Committee) to create healthier, more resilient, and economically empowered communities in eastern DRC.. .Asili 2.0 leverages $7.4 million over five years from private sector partners and further supports administration priorities by increasing the sustainable impact of USAID development objectives through private sector engagement. The activity uses a sustainable, social enterprise approach to deliver an integrated business model for improvement of economic, health, and WASH outcomes. Such outcomes include, for example, improved access to clean water, income-generating activities, and quality health care services for populations living in poverty. The activities are on a fee-for-service basis that provides a stream of revenue to help offset the overall cost of providing clean water, improving hygiene, and administering quality healthcare services..The activity contributes to the Mission's Integrated Country Strategy via Mission Goal 2 (Improved quality of life for Congolese through delivery of core services and expanded economic growth) and USAID's Country Development Cooperation Strategy via Development Objective 3 (Inclusive, broad-based, and sustainable economic growth increased). The activity fundamentally contributes to sustainable economic growth as a protective factor critical to achieve greater regional stability, a U.S. foreign policy priority.

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): To increase youth resilience to the effects of conflict and violence in the eastern DRC, the Integrated Youth Development Activity (IYDA) will employ an integrated approach that includes interventions in education and economic growth. This approach ensures that youth 1) gain and apply relevant skills for improved educational and social outcomes; 2) are positively engaged in community activities; and 3) are engaged in productive, market-linked livelihoods. IYDA will empower a cadre of youth with the assets and the skills to better identify, assess, and create economic opportunities, as well as to make positive life decisions. This activity will facilitate an enabling environment at the community level that supports youth in developing a sense of competence, usefulness, belonging, and empowerment. IYDA will increase the self-efficiency of 10,000 vulnerable youth; provide basic education to 12,000 individuals; support 8,000 young people as they gain work experience; and strengthen the capacity of approximately 690 teachers, facilitators, and youth literacy volunteers. All vulnerable youth receive 12 months of basic education followed by six months of livelihoods and employment support. The life skills and work preparedness curriculum include sexual and reproductive health modules. IYDA provides sensitization and outreach activities on family planning as part of the positive youth development. IYDA will reinforce these pathways, with the ultimate goal of increasing their resilience to conflict and violence. .IYDA advances the Mission's CDCS TO 3 of strengthening the foundation for durable peace in eastern DRC, while feeding into USG's international basic education strategy and USAID's education policy. IYDA also contributes to greater regional stability, a U.S. foreign policy priority. ... .. .. .

title.narrative: Zahabu Safi (The Commercially Viable Conflict-Free Gold Project CVCFG)

description.narrative: Zahabu Safi (The Commercially Viable Conflict-Free Gold Project CVCFG) is an economic development initiative funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The goal of the project is to establish a conflict-free artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) gold supply chain originating from eastern DRC. The five-year program builds on recent successes achieved by donor-funded initiatives to export responsibly-produced gold to jewelry buyers in North America and Europe. This project contributes to the broader US government goal of reducing instability in the DRC which has more than 1,100 minerals worth nearly $24 trillion by providing commercial opportunities to artisanal miners by linking them to responsible gold buyers in international markets, or by strengthening local partnerships between artisanal mining cooperatives and established institutional investors/anchor institutions within the DRC.

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): .The activity addresses illicit markets for conflict minerals associated with many corrupt practices in the provinces of North and South Kivu, including financing armed groups, money laundering, elite capture of resources, illegal taxation, among other areas. By reinforcing government systems that exist in the law, but have never been put into practice, USAID strengthens a critical governance process called mine site qualification and validation, which ensures mine sites meet standards and national and international criteria. This activity promotes additional transparency and accountability by empowering local actors-particularly civil society, communities and provincial and municipal authorities-to implement continuous and rigorous monitoring of minerals. As an alternative to prior methods of validation that relied on infrequent visits from authorities, USAID's current approach decreases the risk of corruption by bolstering training and more frequent involvement from local actors, particularly civil society groups. The project helps to assemble local monitoring committees to facilitate the initial qualification of mine sites as well as monitor sites' ongoing adherence to national regulations. Through ongoing security analysis and monitoring of mine sites, the project increases the capacity of staff from the DRC's Ministry of Mines and strengthens artisanal and small-scale mining cooperatives to address issues like child labor. Through associations of women, FY 2021 funds will raise awareness among local groups of women involved with artisanal mining about the protections provided under existing laws. ..This activity contributes to the Integrated Country Strategy and Country Development Cooperation Strategy via Development Objective 1 "Responsiveness of Public Institutions to Citizens' Needs Improved"..

(Democratic Republic of the Congo): The Access, Reading, Retention, and Accountability (ACCELERE! 4) Phase II: Education in Emergencies activity harmonizes donor collaboration in providing the implementing partner with the capacity to rapidly deploy emergency educational programming interventions to address humanitarian crises and their aftermath in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). .UNICEF, the implementing partner for this mechanism, is the global leader for the Education in Emergencies sector. Their community-based approach and child-friendly school approach are global models and these approaches ensure a child-centered, safe, and protective environment for students. Additionally, UNICEF has developed a renowned peace-building education curriculum, as well as Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian Action-programmatic materials which ensure consistent, high-quality implementation. These approaches and tools, coupled with sustained decades of experience, provide a strong foundation for selecting UNICEF to implement this mechanism..ACCELERE! 4 Phase II: Education in Emergencies advances the USAID DRC Country Development Cooperation Strategy (CDCS) Transition Objective 2 (DO2) by improving lives through coordinated development approaches, while feeding into USAID Education Strategy Goal 3, increased equitable access to education in environments affected by crisis and conflict. ACCELERE! 4 also contributes to greater regional stability, humanitarian response, and improved education, all U.S. foreign policy priorities..

(Democratic Republic of the Congo): Support for strengthened elections and political processes will contribute to freer and fairer elections in the DRC and further establish a culture of democratic electoral reform. With FY 2022 funding, USAID's DRC Electoral Integrity Activity (DEIA) will support the DRC's national electoral commission with the management and organization of the proposed 2023 national elections through training, coaching, and producing organizational resources for electoral staff and poll workers. This activity will also focus on improving civic education, strengthening citizen knowledge and awareness of elections and political processes, empowering communities to participate in elections, and supporting marginalized communities to understand and access these political processes. Another component of this activity will be supporting civil society actors to raise awareness about electoral and political processes and hold the government accountable to promised timelines and procedures surrounding elections..The activity supports Mission Objective 3.1 (Partner with like-minded national and international actors for transparent, inclusive, and timely elections) through technical assistance and training to improve electoral processes, voter education, and civic participation....

(Democratic Republic of the Congo): ...The USAID Media Sector Development Activity (MSDA) will promote an open and vibrant media sector that contributes to more responsive and transparent institutions in the DRC. USAID will: 1) strengthen the legal and regulatory environment for media; 2) support targeted media outlets to become more independent and professional; and 3) increase access to high-quality, public-interest reporting. USAID will train journalists and support civil society and media to promote free and fair 2023 elections in the DRC through countering disinformation and hate speech and ensuring public access to accurate information...FY 2022 funds will support the protection and defense of journalists under threat and strengthen the legal framework to enable free media, open information access, and freedom of expression. Key interventions will strengthen advocacy capacity, digital and physical security awareness, response capabilities, and media networking activities. USAID will promote positive, nonviolent male development to shift attitudes and practices among boys and youth, including a focus on child, early, and forced marriage (CEFM) and gender-based violence (GBV)...MSDA contributes to Mission Objective 3.2 (Improve public institutions' responsiveness, respect for human rights and basic freedoms, and accountability, including through strengthening education overall) by promoting responsive, transparent, and accountable public institutions in the DRC and improving their respect for human rights and basic freedoms through the support of free press..In addition, $250,000 for this IM will meet the control for the Gender Equity and Equality Action (GEEA) Fund. Programming will align with Priority 5: Dismantle Systemic Gender Barriers. USAID will provide robust capacity building for female journalists and women-led media associations to promote critical conversations and create a safe, democratic space for dialogue on women's and girls' issues.. .

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): USAID's Fall Armyworm (FAW) Activity provides technical assistance to help local agricultural system actors deploy an integrated FAW management strategy in the targeted geographical area, enhancing food security, generating income, and improving the livelihoods of smallholder maize producers. Establishing effective feedback loops and substantive consultation between key FAW stakeholders enables USAID to develop an effective FAW Integrated Pest Management (IPM) strategy. In addition, with FY 2022 funding, the activity will enable smallholder maize producers in the DRC to gain equal access to the necessary information, skills, and inputs to safely and effectively manage FAW attacks and increase maize yields through good agricultural practices. Maize is an important staple crop within parts of DRC with the potential to improve nutrition outcomes...Results of this activity include: 1) sustainable and cost-effective IPM technologies developed, validated, and scaled for the local context; 2) increased adoption of good agricultural practices by smallholder maize producers and other local agricultural system actors to control FAW; and 3) appropriate policies and systems to create an enabling environment for the deployment of IPM...By promoting a more resilient private sector maize market, the activity contributes to the Integrated Country Strategy's Mission Objective 2.2 (Expand U.S. investment and economic ties by supporting anti-corruption efforts, enhancing security, promoting transparent governance systems, establishing a more cost-effective regulatory framework, and enabling a more investor-friendly business environment) and USAID's Country Development Cooperation Strategy's Development Objective 3 (Inclusive, broad-based, and sustainable economic growth increased). In addition, this activity supports the Administration's Global Food Security Strategy and Feed the Future goals....

title.narrative: Accelerating Peri-Urban Water and Sanitation Services in Kasai Oriental and Lomami provinces (DRC WASH)

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): .USAID's Accelerating Peri-Urban Water and Sanitation Services in Kasai Oriental and Lomami Provinces Activity aims to increase access to basic water services for 550,000 people and sanitation services for 50,000 people through improved governance and strengthened service provider models. In collaboration with provincial and local entities, FY 2022 funds will support in-kind grant assistance for twenty-nine autonomous Water Service Providers (WSPs). These grants will support the WSPs to accelerate and improve access to drinking water in their respective geographic areas, accelerating the Congolese population's level of service along the water ladder and USAID's Localization Agenda..With FY 2022 funds, grant activities will multiply the number of autonomous WSPs and private sector entities reporting increased recognition of rights by national, provincial, and local leadership and public sector entities and increase the percentage of targeted WSPs exhibiting increased institutional capacity. Through this activity, USAID will strengthen institutional governance in support of water service delivery across all levels of the service ladder and in all technical areas, improve administrative management of the water sector, increase knowledge of the legal and regulatory framework for water resource governance, and promote gender-sensitive water management...This activity will contribute to Mission Objective 4.1 (Strengthen institutional and community capacity to prevent outbreaks from becoming pandemics as well as respond to and overcome frequent public health and humanitarian emergencies) by supporting sustainable water and sanitation systems. Clean water and sanitation prevents many infectious diseases from spreading and promotes healthier, more stable, and productive communities, thereby reducing threats to U.S. national security. This activity advances the U.S. Global Water Strategy, which defines water security as a national security

title.narrative: USAID’s Education is The Response Activity (Elimu ni Jibu ya USAID)

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): DRC has significantly increased access to primary education. The net attendance rate increased from 52 percent in 2001 to 78 percent in 2018, though 7.6 million children aged 5-17 remain out of school. Adolescent girls in conflict settings are especially at risk of sexual and gender-based violence, which often leads to dropping out and further vulnerability. To address these challenges, FY 2022 funding for USAID's Education is the Response will increase children's access to education, create safer learning environments, and improve the quality of teaching and learning in schools. USAID/DRC focuses on girls, boys, and youth living in crisis- and conflict-affected and under-resourced communities...Equal access to quality education can create pathways for economic growth, improved health outcomes, sustained democratic governance, and more peaceful and resilient societies. Education is the Response builds the resilience of Congolese children and youth and provides grants to local organizations focused on child protection and education...USAID's Education is the Response advances the Integrated Country Strategy via Mission Objective 3.2 (Improve public institutions' responsiveness, respect for human rights and basic freedoms, and accountability, including through strengthening education overall) by strengthening community resilience, improving the quality of education services by non-state actors, and increasing the demand for and utilization of quality education......

title.narrative: SASA IVI DRC – Elimination of Tuberculosis Kasaï/ Eastern Congo

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): .SASA IVI - Elimination of Tuberculosis (TB) is one of two USAID activities in the DRC that is a part of the Local Organizations Network. In support of USAID's Global Accelerator to End Tuberculosis, this activity strengthens TB prevention, care, and treatment in six DRC provinces (Kasai Central, Kasai Oriental, Lomami, Sankuru, South Kivu, and Tanganyika) through sub-awards with five local organizations that span civil society organizations, faith-based organizations, private sector service delivery providers, and academic institutions. USAID will provide technical assistance to these local organizations to implement locally generated solutions to improve TB diagnosis, treatment, and prevention..With FY 2022 funds, SASA IVI - Elimination of TB will facilitate new TB partnerships, foster inclusiveness, and promote advocacy, empowerment, and accountability for improved TB services in the DRC. Partnerships under this activity will strengthen local capacity to provide quality, equitable, and lifesaving TB services. This will be achieved by mobilizing and leveraging local resources to reach National TB Program targets and promoting more self-reliant, sustainable, and country-owned TB programming in the DRC...This activity will contribute to Mission Objective 4.1 (Strengthen institutional and community capacity to prevent outbreaks from becoming pandemics as well as respond to and overcome frequent public health and humanitarian emergencies) by increasing country capacity, ownership, and accountability towards a more sustainable and effective TB program for the Congolese population. This activity strengthens DRC's capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to infectious diseases, thereby benefiting U.S. national security interests, and advances USAID's Localization Agenda.... .

title.narrative: USAID's Sustainable Water & Sanitation Systems Activity, North and South Kivu (SWASSA)

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): USAID's Sustainable Water & Sanitation Systems Activity (SWASSA) aims to create sustainable and equitable access to a clean water supply and safe sanitation services through developing the market sector in the Kivus region. Originally, USAID SWASSA envisioned limited infrastructure investment to support performance-based water system management, but after the volcanic eruption in 2021, it increased infrastructure investments to accommodate multi-donor water infrastructure support activities..With FY 2022 funds, USAID SWASSA will provide critical water supply to residents in the peri-urban area of Goma by delivering a large water storage upgrade project, designing and constructing a pumping station. The activity will also support targeted training. USAID SWASSA will promote climate change adaptation measures by increasing the energy efficiency of electromechanical equipment to reduce operators' running costs, establishing bypasses in reservoir systems in case of earthquake damage, creating systems redundancies to avoid service interruption resulting from potential lava flow damage, and diversifying power supply sources..This activity will contribute to Mission Objective 4.1 (Strengthen institutional and community capacity to prevent outbreaks from becoming pandemics as well as respond to and overcome frequent public health and humanitarian emergencies) by supporting sustainable water and sanitation systems. Clean water and sanitation prevents many infectious diseases from spreading and promotes healthier, more stable, and productive communities, thereby reducing threats to U.S. national security. This activity also supports the U.S. Global Water Strategy, the USAID Water and Sanitation Development Plan, and the USAID Climate Strategy...

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): With FY 2022 funds, USAID's Strengthening Livelihoods and Resilience (SLR) Activity will support inclusive agricultural growth, improve the nutritional status of women and children, and increase resilience in targeted communities in Ituri Province in eastern DRC. It will build resilience by promoting expanded and diversified market-oriented livelihood opportunities, increasing private sector activity and investments in the sector, improving access to finance for smallholder farmers, improving land tenure, and integrating with other USAID-supported activities to promote nutrition-sensitive approaches to market-systems development. As USAID SLR develops and tests models and provides technical assistance, the activity will contribute to a better understanding of the needs of vulnerable populations and how they can better adapt to re-occurring shocks, such as emerging plant diseases, increased conflict, and climatic events. Given the prevalence of women in the agriculture sector and their critical role in improving their families' nutritional status, health, and livelihoods, USAID SLR will also promote improved nutrition practices with women's groups. The activity will focus on developing interventions to empower and increase women's participation in agricultural markets, such as improving access to credit, inputs, and agricultural training..The activity will contribute to the Integrated Country Strategy's Mission Objective 2.2 (Expand U.S. investment and economic ties by supporting anti-corruption efforts, enhancing security, promoting transparent governance systems, establishing a more cost-effective regulatory framework, and enabling a more investor-friendly business environment) and USAID's Country Development Cooperation Strategy's Development Objective 3 (Inclusive, broad-based, and sustainable economic growth increased). USAID SLR will be aligned with the Agency's Resilience Policy and the Administration's Global Food Security

title.narrative: USAID Central Africa Regional Third Party Monitoring (CART) project

description.narrative: This three-year USAID Central Africa Regional Third Party Monitoring (CART) project will establish independent, impartial, timely, responsive, contextualized, and forward-looking third party monitoring (TPM) and operational support services. CART will provide a comprehensive range of verification and outcome monitoring, and learning services that will increase USAID's Bureau of Humanitarian Assistance and its implementing partners' (IP) understanding of the outputs, outcomes, progress, challenges, successes, results, and lessons learned for both emergency and non-emergency activities within CAR, DRC and ROC. This project seeks to improve USAID/BHA's capability to utilize humanitarian assistance resources to ameliorate the drivers of poverty and malnutrition characterized by complex emergencies within the region.

title.narrative: USAID’s End Malaria Project (Malaria Insecticide Treated Net (ITN) Distribution)

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): Malaria remains the single greatest cause of illness and death in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), killing around 22,800 Congolese in 2021. Preventive malaria interventions are an important, cost-effective step in tackling DRC's high malaria burden, and insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) are a highly effective means of preventing infection and reducing malaria transmission. USAID's End Malaria Activity will use FY 2022 funds to distribute ITNs through mass campaigns and school-based distribution in targeted provinces. It will also strengthen the capacity of the National Malaria Control Program to plan and execute ITN distribution. All mass distribution campaigns will use a door-to-door strategy instead of large awareness-raising events to minimize the spread of COVID-19 by avoiding mass gatherings. In addition, all actors involved in distribution will wear face masks, use hand sanitizer, and observe social distancing...This activity will contribute to Mission Objective 4.1 (Strengthen institutional and community capacity to prevent outbreaks from becoming pandemics as well as respond to and overcome frequent public health and humanitarian emergencies) by supporting the DRC's goal to accelerate a reduction in maternal and child deaths. Healthy women and children contribute to more productive, self-reliant, and stable communities, thereby maximizing American taxpayer investments and reducing threats to U.S. national security.....

(Democratic Republic of the Congo): .USAID's DRC Invest activity aims to unlock $100 million in capital for Congolese agribusinesses and other enterprises. In addition to unlocking capital, DRC Invest attracts new impact investors to DRC, sustainably increasing Congolese businesses' access to favorable financing to fuel business growth..With FY 2021 funds, DRC Invest identifies small and medium-sized businesses to increase their capacity and assist them with financing through an investment facilitation platform. In turn, these businesses benefit local communities and producers as they strengthen key sectors and value chains. DRC Invest helps deepen DRC's nascent financial markets and improves the business and investment ecosystem. The platform provides technical assistance to facilitate and expedite engagement between small businesses and risk-adverse finance providers. By utilizing market-led impact investment models, the activity strengthens the sustainability of investments in communities and regions that lack well-financed, resilient market systems..The activity contributes to the Mission's Integrated Country Strategy via Mission Goal 2 (Improved quality of life for Congolese through delivery of core services and expanded economic growth) and USAID's Country Development Cooperation Strategy via Development Objective 3 (Inclusive, broad-based, and sustainable economic growth increased). The activity fundamentally contributes to sustainable economic growth as facts that can further stimulate regional stability and enable economic growth, a critical U.S. foreign policy priority..

(Democratic Republic of the Congo): .USAID Reduce Tuberculosis (TB) is one of two USAID activities in the DRC that is a part of the Local Organizations Network. In support of USAID's Global Accelerator to End Tuberculosis, this activity facilitates and sustains new partnerships, fosters inclusiveness, and promotes advocacy, empowerment, and accountability for improved TB service delivery in the DRC..USAID Reduce TB will use FY 2022 funds to equip local communities and health service providers in three provinces (Haut-Katanga, Haut-Lomami, and Lualaba) to better manage and deliver TB prevention, treatment, and care interventions. The activity will collaborate with the Ministry of Health and provincial TB coordination structures to identify TB cases and support TB patients and their households to successfully complete treatment and initiate preventive therapy. Partnerships with local organizations, including civil society organizations, faith-based organizations, private sector service delivery providers, and academic institutions, will drive the implementation of locally developed solutions to improve TB diagnosis, treatment, and prevention services, which advances USAID's Localization Agenda...This activity will contribute to Mission Objective 4.1 (Strengthen institutional and community capacity to prevent outbreaks from becoming pandemics as well as respond to and overcome frequent public health and humanitarian emergencies) by increasing country capacity, ownership, and accountability towards a more sustainable and effective TB program for the Congolese population. This activity strengthens DRC's capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to infectious diseases, thereby benefiting U.S. national security interests....

title.narrative: USAID’s We’re Reading Activity (Sasa Tunasoma ya USAID)

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): Congolese children and youth, particularly the most marginalized, face multiple barriers to acquiring foundational literacy skills. Despite these challenges, Congolese value education and, when resources and education opportunities are available, families prioritize education. Education is valued as a pathway out of cycles of poverty, conflict, and instability. The Congolese government has identified improving education as a top priority...With FY 2022 funds, USAID's We're Reading will leverage USAID's prior experience supporting foundational learning to ensure that children aged six to nine in select marginalized and underserved zones of South Kivu gain foundational literacy and social and emotional skills, enabling them to function in school at a second grade level or higher...USAID will achieve results by engaging community leaders and parents. It will provide safe spaces, contextually-relevant materials, and multiple learning pathways for children who have had limited access to formal schooling, especially girls, indigenous children (pygmies), and children with disabilities. This intervention adopts a modular implementation approach, whereby result packages may be activated or deactivated based on contextual and operational constraints, opportunities, and learning results...We're Reading will advance the Integrated Country Strategy via Mission Objective 3.2 (Improve public institutions' responsiveness, respect for human rights and basic freedoms, and accountability, including through strengthening education overall) by improving education services delivery, increasing access to education services, and strengthening partnership between education actors. It addresses the Administration policy priority of diversity, equity, and inclusion by targeting marginalized groups, including girls, indigenous children, and children with disabilities..

title.narrative: Let's Learn Together ( Apprendre tous Ensemble)

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): Congolese children and youth, particularly the most marginalized, face multiple barriers to acquiring foundational skills, such as reading, literacy, and social and emotional development. Despite these barriers, Congolese value education and, when resources and education opportunities are available, families prioritize education...Similar to USAID's We're Reading, but implemented in different geographic zones, with FY 2022 funds, Let's Learn Together will leverage USAID's prior experience in supporting improved reading, literacy, and social and emotional learning outcomes. It will ensure that children aged six to nine in select marginalized and underserved zones in equateur, Maniema, Tanganyika, and Kinshasa gain foundational literacy and social and emotional skills, enabling them to function in school at a second grade level or higher. USAID will achieve results by engaging community leaders and parents and providing safe spaces, contextually-relevant materials, and multiple learning pathways for children who have had limited access to formal schooling, especially girls, indigenous children, and children with disabilities. Key adaptation and learning events will be identified throughout the life of the activity in order to identify opportunities for revision and forward planning...Let's Learn Together will advance the Integrated Country Strategy via Mission Objective 3.2 (Improve public institutions' responsiveness, respect for human rights and basic freedoms, and accountability, including through strengthening education overall) by improving education services delivery, increasing access to education services, and strengthening partnership between education actors. It addresses the Administration policy priority of diversity, equity, and inclusion by targeting marginalized groups, including girls, indigenous children, and children with disabilities. ...

USAID ESPOIR 2030-Lualaba will work with the government of the DRC (gDRC) and other USAID implementing partners to deliver high quality, accessible HIV/AIDS related services towards achieving HIV epidemic control. This award will focus on service delivery in fourteen (14) health zones in Lualaba province. The recipient will align their activities with the joint United Nations program on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDs) 95-95-95 approach, which sets ambitious treatment targets to end the aids epidemic by 2030. The service delivery model includes all aspects of HIV epidemic control, orphans and vulnerable children (OVC) and some key populations (KPS) programming, to ensure smooth transition of the Existing Key Populations Program (EPIC). The activity will strengthen the integration of HIV/tuberculosis (TB) services, screening and management of co-occurring conditions including other opportunistic infectious and non-communicable diseases; and provide direct, comprehensive services to OVC.

The activity that will focus on service delivery to support existing implementers in PEPFAR supported provinces with progressive expansion over the life of the activity. In year 1, the activity will start in Lualaba and will then expand to Haut-Katanga according to the needs. This service delivery activity will include all aspects of the HIV epidemic control of key and vulnerable populations (female sex workers [FSW] and their clients and their kids, men who have sex with men [MSM], transgender, people who inject drugs and people in prison).
Reduce the transmission and impact of HIV/AIDS through support for prevention, care and treatment programs.

title.narrative: Legalizing and Formalizing the Artisanal Cobalt Sector

description.narrative: In partnership with Enterprise Generale du Cobalt (EGC) and the Responsible Minerals Initiative (RMI), USAID funding will support the operationalization of EGC's field operations by piloting a new model of legalizing and formalizing the artisanal cobalt sector. If successful, the model can be scaled to other sites and regions of the country. The Impact Facility co-founded and serves as the secretariat of the Fair Cobalt Alliance (FCA), a multi-stakeholder initiative that brings together 20+ actors from across the cobalt supply chain, including industrial miners, battery manufacturers, downstream companies, and other non-profit organizations. EGC was established in 2019 by government decree. EGC's role is to export artisanal cobalt and strategic minerals and ensure that this production meets high standards of social and environmental responsibility and traceability.

The goal of the activity is to support highly impoverished urban areas of Goma, Nord Kivu, DRC through the rising generation of young adolescent girls in creating resilient, safe, and socially cohesive communities.

From 2006-2011, IMA World Health led Project AXxes, a large USAID-funded health systems strengthening and service delivery program targeting eight million people in post-conflict areas of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The main objective was to improve the availability, quality, and capacity of overall health care, using the appui global or global assistance strategy of the Ministry of Health (MOH), in 57 rural health zones adversely affected by years of civil war, neglect, and relative isolation. Approximately two-thirds of the health zones were nonfunctional or had limited services at project startup. The projects assistance focused foremost on the MOH priority package of primary health care (PHC) interventions including reinforcement of vaccination services, provision of pharmaceuticals and supplies to hospitals and health centers, delivery of a full complement of maternal and child health services including family planning, and newborn and postpartum care.

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

Strengthen the legal, regulatory, institutional, and information environment which protects and enables the growth in associational life and the development of independent and sustainable civil society organizations (CSOs). Build the capacity of civil society organizations to act as agents for reform and support their participation in democratic decision-making through articulating and representing their members interests, engaging in service delivery, and advocating for issues which become part of the public agenda and are reflected in public policies. Encourage the strengthening of a civic culture which supports democratic institutions and processes, active participation in political and civic life, and the civic virtues of tolerance, pluralism, compromise, trust, and respect for individual rights, including gender equality.

In AMPATH's definition of "healthcare," the focus is on the patient, not the disease. If a patient is hungry, or without a job, or is the victim of discrimination or abuse, AMPATH will respond, a commitment that leads inexorably toward holistic care. Therefore, AMPATH not only treats over 140,000 HIV-positive persons atover 60urban and rural clinic sites throughout western Kenya. We also partner with the UN World Food Programme to feed 31,000 HIV-affected persons daily, provide school fees, nutrition, and other assistance over 20,000 children left orphaned or vulnerable due to HIV/AIDS, and have enrolled 10,000-plus patients in income security programs, including agricultural extension services, micro-finance and small business initiatives. We also conduct prevention and early treatment programs that demonstrate a community-based effort that can virtually halt the spread of HIV/AIDS.

description.narrative: Improve the capacity and sustainability of civil and criminal justice sector actors and institutions, enhance coordination amongst them, develop citizen demand for an effective and accountable justice system, and develop associations to advocate for all citizens. Justice sector actors and institutions include: police, border security, prosecutors, forensics experts, judges, court personnel, public defenders, corrections personnel, private bar, law schools, legal professional associations, and training institutions for each of them. Work towards an equitable justice system by ensuring equality before the law, fair trial standards, and other elements of procedural fairness. Ensure more equitable access to justice through innovations within and beyond the state system and through improvements in the quality and quantity of justice services, with a particular focus on women, youth, the poor, and other marginalized or vulnerable groups. Programs primarily focused on trafficking in persons or migrant smuggling should be included in element 5.3 under the Transnational Crime area in the Peace and Security Objective.

title.narrative: Ushindi - Overcoming Sexual and Gender-Based Violence in Eastern Congo

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): The Ushindi activity addresses sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) in eastern DRC through a holistic approach to assist survivors of SGBV and engage communities in long-term attitude change. Ushindi covers a population of 1.3 million in 10 health zones to: 1) provide SGBV survivors with quality, age-appropriate medical care, psychological counseling, and legal support; 2) improve communities' response to SGBV in order to facilitate rape survivors' recovery; 3) improve survivors' social integration and economic recovery; and 4) strengthen individuals' and community-based organizations' ability to prevent SGBV.

title.narrative: Prevention of and Protection Against Sexual and Gender-Based Violence Using Behavior Change Communication "BCC"

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): The Prevention of SGBV using Behavior Change Communication (BCC) activity increases community prevention of SGBV and reinforces and sustains positive behaviors in eastern DRC. Implementing partners (International Medical Corps and Search For Common Ground) decrease GBV through: reducing stigma associated with rape; increasing awareness in families and communities of the consequences of GBV and the need to support survivors; and increasing capacity of local organizations, including religious leaders and local government, to deliver social services and conduct advocacy. Annually, more than 1.6 million individuals are reached by mass media BCC campaigns. In order to sustain and reinforce positive behaviors, individuals learn to promote non-violence and to reward those behaviors. BCC training is provided to teachers, religious and community leaders, and police officers to promote GBV prevention and improve response to incidents of GBV.

title.narrative: Media Sector Development Program (MSDP) in the Democratic Republic of Congo

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): The Media Sector Development Program (MSDP), implemented by Internews Network, promotes an independent, objective, professional, and sustainable media sector in the DRC. The activity improves the quality of journalism and news production, and enhances the management capacity of community radio stations and local radio networks in target provinces by providing training in marketing and financial management, mentoring, technical assistance, and material support. The activity also strengthens the legal framework supporting media at the national level and advocates for media regulatory reform.By the end of MSDP in 2015, targeted community radio stations and networks will have enhanced management and financial systems, as well as improved reporting and news production. In addition modifications to legislation and regulations upholding press freedoms and protections are expected to be introduced in Parliament.

description.narrative: Developing and Strengthening Services and Systems that Support Family Cohesion and Respond to the Separation of Children in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) The objective of this program is to develop and strengthen systems to support the protection and wellbeing of children and families and to prevent and respond to family separation.

(Democratic Republic of the Congo): The Presidential Malaria Initiative (PMI) Expansion activity covers 68 health zones in five provinces and reaches over 10 million people. This activity aims to decrease morbidity and mortality due to malaria by 50 percent in intervention areas by focusing on four essential components: malaria prevention with provision of long-lasting insecticidal nets and preventative treatment for pregnant women; diagnosis and treatment of simple and severe cases of malaria; cross-cutting activities including behavior change communications, supply chain management, and monitoring and evaluation; and local capacity building. With FY~2015 funds, PMI Expansion will train and support the supervision of facility and community based health workers and lab technicians, support National Malaria Control Program (NMCP) provincial malaria officers, and transport commodities to service delivery points.

description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

title.narrative: Roads to a Healthy Future II (ROADS II) - Democratic Republic of the Congo (Phase 1)

description.narrative: The Roads to a Healthy Future (ROADS II) project aims to reduce potential HIV transmission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) among people living in and traveling along the transport corridors that link artisanal and industrial mining communities in East and Southern Africa. The program complements current work supported by the U.S. Agency for International Development in Katanga and Orientale provinces by introducing a package of HIV services that are carefully tailored to the needs of at-risk populations, including truck drivers, artisanal miners, female sex workers, girls and young women engaged in transactional sex and other people who are vulnerable to infection.

(Democratic Republic of the Congo): USAID will continue supporting the GDA between the Catholic Relief Services and GlaxoSmithKline Services Unlimited that funds the "Afya Mama na Mtoto" activity (Healthy Babies and Mothers). This activity aims to reduce the neonatal and maternal mortality in 34 health facilities in South-Kivu. Through its two technical arms, health facilities and community, the mechanism provides basic equipment for resuscitation, essential medicines, staff training, and increases community awareness. It also strengthens the capacity of health center staff to respond to babies who are unable to breathe on their own at birth by promoting the "Helping Babies Breathe" curriculum. Moreover, it improves the stewardship function of the health zone management team. By providing these interventions, the activity ensures that babies gain timely access to lifesaving health care.

title.narrative: Rice As A Tool To Improve Lives In The Democratic Republic Of Congo

description.narrative: Rice is critical to the food security and economy of the Democratic Republic of the Congos capital city of Kinshasa. This USAID-funded program aims to improve the local rice supply chain through a variety of steps; these include increasing the productivity of small farmers, improving post-harvest processing and handling of rice and strengthening farmer associations and cooperatives.

title.narrative: Integrated HIV/AIDS Project in Haut Katanga and Lualaba (IHAP-HK/L)

description.narrative: This activity will work with the Government of the DRC (GDRC) to strengthen the continuum of care1 for quality HIV/AIDS services in select health zones to achieve epidemic control. This will be one of the main implementing mechanisms for the Presidents Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) in the DRC.

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): This activity ensures the continuum of care for HIV/AIDS services. It increases the utilization of integrated HIV/AIDS services at both facility- and community-based levels. It also strengthens health systems to increase access to services and improve health outcomes for people living with HIV/AIDS, as well as for the general population from the catchment area. .Building on the PEPFAR-supported platform, FY 2020 family planning funds will ensure integration of family planning services within broader HIV prevention, testing, and counseling services; treatment services for people living with HIV/AIDS, as well as other people seeking general primary health care within these health facilities; and comprehensive prevention of mother to child transmission services at all supported HIV facilities. The activity will support training and supervision of family planning providers and technical assistance to improve provider skill for family planning services. The integrated HIV and family planning services will lead to improved health outcomes and resilient communities, thus contributing to DRC's Journey to Self Reliance... .. .

The goal of the Education Evaluation and Assessment Services is to provide the USAID/DRC Education Office and Mission with information to inform program implementation. The services will provide baseline data in target provinces, equated instruments for future data collection, and consultant services for needed assessments related to local language instruction and cost models of implementation. These services meet the Missions purpose to acquire surveys, studies, and research which provide specific information to USAID for its direct activities. a) EdData II BPAThis independent collection of data will serve as the baseline for the new Room to Learn service delivery activity. The evaluation services requested from the Contractor has three objectives: 1. Use the EGRA, Early Grade Math Assessment (EGMA), and Snapshot of School Management Effectiveness (SSME) tools to (a) support dialogue with MEPSP, parents and other education stakeholders on the critical need to focus on early grade reading, math, and school management effectiveness and (b) improve instruction; 2. Build the capacity of the MEPSP in designing and conducting the EGRA, EGMA, and SSME with the aim of institutionalizing assessment in the early grades and focusing school management on improving learning outcomes; and3. Provide strategic analysis that explores links between EGRA, EGMA, and SSME.

title.narrative: Empowering Adolescent Girls to Learn through Education (EAGLE)

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): USAID's EAGLE activity prepares adolescent girls in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to forge their futures through integrated programming in education, health, and gender in peri-urban areas. USAID provides instruction in reading, writing, and mathematics through formal school curriculum and after-school tutoring, as well as professional development for educators on improved pedagogy. The activity also increases the number of girls who transition into and complete secondary school. EAGLE's gender-transformative approach engages girls, boys, women, and men in actively examining and changing entrenched gender norms that harm individuals and hinder social and economic development. Activities improve awareness about HIV/AIDS and health, build self-esteem and leadership skills, develop effective communication skills, and provide tutoring, mentoring, and youth discussion clubs while mobilizing communities to develop gender-responsive school improvement plans.

(Democratic Republic of the Congo): The Access, Reading, Retention and Accountability (ACCELERE!1) Activity improves equitable access to education and learning outcomes for girls and boys in 26 sub-educational provinces in the DRC. FY 2019 resources will improve reading and writing for at least 320,000 girls and boys across 1,600 private schools in four local languages (Kiswahili, Lingala, Ciluba, and Oral French), and support the training of 6,500 teachers and school directors during Year 5 of the project; provide access to primary schooling for 100,000 out-of-school children; increase student retention in targeted schools by 20 percent; and strengthen capacities of parent committees, school management committees, and school communities especially to support private and religious schools, private centres de rattrapage scolaire (CRSs), and centres d'apprentissage professionnel (CAPs). It will also support 200 non-formal alternative/ accelerated learning programs and vocational training for out-of-school youth. Specifically, ACCELERE!1 will provide in-kind grants to CSOs who then, in turn, will support vulnerable households to cover school fees through the Income Generating Activities (IGA) and ''Community Savings Plans" (AVEC) mechanisms. Additionally, ACCELERE! 1 collaborates, with national and provincial education authorities to develop teaching and learning materials and improve education governance and accountability. .ACCELERE!1 advances the USAID/DRC's DO 2 of improved lives through coordinated development approaches, while feeding into USAID's Education Strategy Goal 1, improved early grade reading. ACCELERE!1 also contributes to increasing education and skills to further economic growth and private sector, a U.S. foreign policy priority. ...... .

(Democratic Republic of the Congo): The Integrated Governance Activity (IGA) will strengthen governance in targeted service delivery entities and enhance the social contract between citizens and their government in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The activity will empower citizens, civil society, and the private sector to hold government institutions accountable through improved oversight of public service delivery in health, education and economic growth. The activity will emphasize public financial management, mostly promoting participatory budget processes and citizen oversight and will complement ongoing Congolese and other efforts to ensure that local, provincial, and national revenues are managed more transparently and employed to address citizen priorities, especially in Ebola affected areas. Assistance will include government entities. .IGA contributes to Mission Objective 1.2 by empowering national-level institutions to more effectively implement their mandates and Mission Objective 2.1 by improving public service delivery in health, education and economic growth. IGA works to advance the Administration's policy priority of protecting America's security at home and abroad by addressing a key driver of instability in the DRC - poor governance and weak institutions. By doing so, IGA will also support efforts to respond to the Ebola outbreak by addressing the underlying governance weaknesses that hinder the Ebola response. ... .

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): The TBD Value Chains activity will aim to increase household incomes and access to nutrient-rich crops and cash crops by linking smallholder farmers to strengthened and inclusive value chains and supportive market services. The activity's focus is improved efficiency and inclusiveness of these value chains and expanded access to agricultural inputs, transportation, and financial services.. .FY 2021 funds will strengthen cooperative capacity, organize farmers into groups for training on improved post-harvest techniques and crop quality, facilitate access to finance, and improve market access. As one of several USAID activities co-located in South Kivu province, the TBD Value Chains activity will build upon and leverage complementary Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance Resilience Food Security Activities (RFSAs), health activities, and USAID's coordinated investments in governance. As a result, thousands of households will benefit from improved access to agricultural inputs and market systems...The TBD Value Chains activity will build the capacity and resilience of vulnerable populations to respond to shocks and stresses and take advantage of economic opportunities, contributing to the Mission's Integrated Country Strategy via Mission Goal 2 (Improved quality of life for Congolese through delivery of core services and expanded economic growth) and USAID's Country Development Cooperation Strategy via Development Objective 3 (Inclusive, broad-based, and sustainable economic growth increased). By supporting inclusive agricultural growth, improving the nutritional status of women and children, and increasing resilience in targeted communities, the activity will also support the Administration's Global Food Security Strategy and Feed the Future goals..

title.narrative: Bokengi Bwa Maponami Elections Observation Activity (BBM II)

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): FY 2018 resources will be provided to the Episcopal Peace and Justice Commission (CEJP) of the Catholic Church to continue to bolster its organizational and technical capacity to conduct long and short-term domestic elections observation in accordance with international standards for elections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Key expected results include: 1) an enhanced capacity of the CEJP to conduct domestic observation activities; 2) improved CEJP ability to effectively report on the electoral process and elections-related violence before, during, and after elections; 3) impartial observation of the upcoming electoral process; and 4) wide awareness and understanding among Congolese citizens and national and international actors as to the quality and credibility of the electoral process. This activity contributes to Mission Objective 1.1 by promoting credible and inclusive national, provincial, and local elections through domestic observation. BBM II also works to advance the Administration's policy priority of protecting America's security at home and abroad by addressing a key driver of instability in the DRC - poor governance and weak institutions.

title.narrative: Increase Access to Education for Out-of-School Children

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): .Through this mechanism, USAID will improve school readiness and primary education opportunities for 310,500 children (of which 50 percent are girls) in Katanga and Equateur provinces, including specific marginalized groups (children with disabilities and children without a permanent home living on riversides). This program will establish 100 foundational classes (kindergarten) to enroll 10,500 children and enroll 300,000 out of school vulnerable children in 1,000 primary schools. The program will ensure these children benefit from additional learning support and improved teaching practices. USAID will also strengthen the capacity of national counterparts to address issues facing out-of-school children by building systems, collecting data, reporting outcomes, and helping them to implement programs that support national expansion of proven interventions....

title.narrative: Global Financing Facility (GFF) Multi Donor Trust Fund

description.narrative: USAID/Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the World Bank/DRC are combining resources to support the DRC Ministry of Health's program on Health System Strengthening for Better Maternal and Child Health Results. The objective of this project is to improve the utilization and quality of maternal and child health services in targeted areas. This will be achieved by increasing the availability of a minimum package of services as well as by strengthening the management of the health commodity supply chain. Specifically, USAID's resources will support the institutionalization of performance-based financing and joint solutions with the World Bank to address bottlenecks to health commodities supply chain management.

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): C-Change is a social and behavioral change communication (SBCC) activity increasing positive health behaviors through evidence-based programming. C-Change improves coordination, participation, and country ownership of national health programs by facilitating SBCC technical working groups to plan and implement national programming and building host country and implementing partner skills to design, implement, and evaluate SBCC programs, resulting in more effective and sustainable programming. C-Change addresses behaviors related to malaria, MNCH, WASH, FP, TB, and GBV to increase positive health behaviors and equitable access to health care. In FY 2014, it will emphasize the integration of SBCC programming across sectors and work with the MOH to develop a national HIV communication strategy. C-Change will also support the national FP coordination group during this critical early stage in implementation of the new FP National Strategy 2014-2020.

The Congo Demokrasia project helps build a more fair and transparent democracy within the Democratic Republic of the Congo by increasing voter participation. We are building the capacity of local organizations to deliver voter education programs that help citizens make informed voting decisions and participate actively and peacefully in elections. The project specifically looks to increase the civic engagement of women, youth, religious groups and indigenous populations.

title.narrative: Advancing Human Rights and Promoting Electoral Justice

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): The Advancing Human Rights and Promoting Electoral Justice Activity will protect and promote universally recognized human rights in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) by bolstering the capacity of civil society actors and human rights defenders to monitor and report human rights abuses, including sexual and gender based violence and electoral violence. FY 2018 resources will provide legal assistance to those seeking legal remedies, including vulnerable populations; raise citizens' awareness of their rights; and advocate to authorities for reform through evidence-based policy recommendations. Key expected results include: establishment of alert and protection networks; creation of open source monitoring software to track human rights abuses; training for courts and the National Independent Electoral Commission in the adjudication of election disputes; and creation of an alternative election dispute resolution mechanisms to address electoral challenges at the community level..

(Democratic Republic of the Congo): .The USAID Solutions for Peace and Recovery (SPR) award develops and implements activities with local partners that build peace and stability in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. USAID will use FY 2018 resources to address the root causes of violence leading to political destabilization in eastern DRC. Main activities will include strengthening the capacity of women and marginalized group to participate in decision-making processes, linking women and marginalized groups to decision-making structures to ensure their inclusion in governance, working to change attitudes and norms for greater inclusion, but also expanding access to community and individual resources while improving social cohesion. The USAID Solutions for Peace and Recovery (SPR) is vital for building the foundation for durable peace in Eastern DRC, essential to achieve US Foreign Policy priority... .

title.narrative: Voter Opinion and Involvement through Civic Education Program (VOICE)

description.narrative: The Voter Opinion and Involvement through Civic Education (VOICE) project to improve the capacity of citizens to participate in decentralization and electoral processes. The project reaches underrepresented populations to encourage engagement with broader society, particularly in political participation. IFES initiatives include projects in voter registration, public awareness campaigns, capacity building for local organizations and efforts to motivate vulnerable and marginalized populations to be actively involved in their governance.

title.narrative: Promoting Stabilization and Community Reintegration Project (PSCRP)

description.narrative: PSCRPs purpose was to Enhance reconciliation and recovery in targeted communities in Eastern DRC. The project is implemented by MSI in partnership with International Alert over 26 months from October 2009 until November 2011. PSCRP is a community reconciliation and recovery project using a community-driven development (CDD) methodology, with a cross-cutting conflict-sensitive approach. It supports 30 communities in Eastern DRC, totaling an estimated 280,000 inhabitants.The project is fully funded by USAID. The project was designed and implemented in the context of a new paradigm of stabilization in Eastern DRC, initiated by the UN, and to which USAID wanted to contribute through, amongst other, this project.

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): This program's primary objective is to reduce the food insecurity of vulnerable populations in Katanga and South Kivu Provinces. This is achieved through Mother Leaders and Care Groups to improve nutrition and Farmer Field and Life Groups to promote improved agriculture. Major activities include rehabilitation of irrigation canals, distribution of goats and ducks, training on farming and animal husbandry techniques, value chains analysis, dissemination of agricultural marketing messages via billboard, promotion of sound nutrition and hygiene behavior, and improved access to credit. By 2016, the program will reduce food insecurity among 163,726 people in Katanga and South-Kivu and decrease the percentages of underweight children by 15 percent and stunted children by 10 percent.

title.narrative: South Kivu Development Food Aid Program

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): The goal of the South Kivu Development Food Aid Program (DFAP) is to improve the food security, health, and nutrition of target populations and enable individuals to take advantage of local and regional economic opportunities through greater integration in select value chains. The program will reduce the food insecurity of vulnerable households by promoting improved natural resource management and agricultural production techniques, increased agricultural production and incomes, and farmers' market integration in South Kivu Province. The South Kivu DFAP engages communities and uses community-based, participatory approaches to sustainably increase community water and sanitation access and improve hygiene (WASH) practices. The activity will also support good health and nutrition practices, and reduce chronic malnutrition that results in the stunting of children's physical growth. This activity will work in conjunction with other Mission economic growth and health programs, particularly the Feed the Future Strengthening Value Chains Program. By reducing food insecurity, this activity will contribute to strengthening durable peace in DRC, which is a foreign policy objective...

title.narrative: Tanganyika and South Kivu Development Food Aid Program

description.narrative: (Democratic Republic of the Congo): The goal of this activity is to build resilience and improve food, nutrition, and income security in vulnerable populations by enabling beneficiaries to mitigate and adapt to shocks (including environmental such as crop disease or floods, social such as conflict or insecurity, and economic such as price fluctuations) and identify and take advantage of economic opportunities. The program will reduce food insecurity by promoting improved natural resource management and agricultural production techniques, increased agricultural production and incomes, and market integration in Tanganyika and South Kivu Provinces. This activity engages communities and uses community-based, participatory approaches to increase water and sanitation access and improve hygiene practices. The activity will support good health and nutrition practices and reduce chronic malnutrition that results in the stunting of children's physical growth. This activity will work in conjunction with other Mission economic growth and health programs to reduce food insecurity and contribute to strengthening durable peace in DRC, which is a foreign policy objective.

title.narrative: PREP and incremental funding for Development Food Assistance Program (DFAP) in DRC, Budikadidi

description.narrative: FFP is funding a USAID Implementing Partner to implement the Budikadidi Development Food Security Activity, which seeks to improve the food security, nutritional status, and socio-economic wellbeing of vulnerable households and communities in Kasai Oriental Province. As part of Budikadidi, the Implementing Partner implements a number of complementary interventions across five sectorsagriculture; health and nutrition; water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH); gender; and governancetargeting 580,947 beneficiaries. With FFP support, the Implementing Partner helps to build local capacity, strengthen service-delivery systems, increase accountability, and reduce structural, cultural, and gender-based barriers to sustainable change.

In the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), PATH and our partners are working from the ground up to better link people to HIV and other health services through the five-year ProVIC project. Our programmatic approach includes working through champion communities to link people with integrated HIV prevention, care, and support services.

title.narrative: Advancing Social Marketing for Health in the DRC

description.narrative: The Advance Social Marketing for Health in Democratic Republic of the Congo had the following objectives: 1) Increase the supply and diversity of health products and services that are to be distributed and delivered through the private sector, in conjunction with the public sector, for disease prevention and control as well as integrated health service delivery. 2) Increase the awareness and demand for health products and services to emphasize prevention of childhood illnesses, unintended and unsafe pregnancies, HIV infections and STIs, and to build an informed, sustainable consumer base. 3) Develop and or enhance the ability of the commercial/private sector entities to socially market health products and services including behavior change communication activities. 4) Integrate service delivery and other activities, emphasizing prevention, at national, provincial, district, facility, and community levels through joint planning with the GRDC, other United States Government (USG), and non-USG partners.

USAID is funding the American Refugee Committee's "Creating Community Driven Social Enterprise Zones in eastern DRC" to test and demonstrate an innovative approach to improve child survival and maternal health within a fragile development context. The activity includes health, nutrition/agriculture, and water components that ultimately aim to reduce child mortality and morbidity among children under five and promote maternal health in eastern Congo.The American Refugee Committee and its partners will install a social enterprise zone rationale, results framework, and theory of change during the initial year of the program that will, over time, enhance child survival outcomes in DRC. USAID will continue to enlarge the platform of collaboration and synergy with its partners working in the same geographic area.

title.narrative: Displaced and recent Returnee households Invite Recovery in Eastern DRC (DRIVE)

description.narrative: Displaced and Recent Returnee Households Invite Recovery in Eastern DRC (DRIVE) program addressed basic needs of the most vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host communities. To meet households daily food and NFI needs, households received a comprehensive food and nonfood items assistance package through voucher fairs or direct distributions. A secondary goal was to support the local economys recovery. Finally, the DRIVE response integrated cash-for-work interventions to reinforce intra-community linkages, strengthen community assets and avoid further depletion of host community and host family assets.

description.narrative: Strengthen the legal, regulatory, institutional, and information environment which protects and enables the growth in associational life and the development of independent and sustainable civil society organizations (CSOs). Build the capacity of civil society organizations to act as agents for reform and support their participation in democratic decision-making through articulating and representing their members interests, engaging in service delivery, and advocating for issues which become part of the public agenda and are reflected in public policies. Encourage the strengthening of a civic culture which supports democratic institutions and processes, active participation in political and civic life, and the civic virtues of tolerance, pluralism, compromise, trust, and respect for individual rights, including gender equality.
